newsitem.title: USA: Summer weather promotes Florida citrus growth-FASS.
newsitem.headline: Summer weather promotes Florida citrus growth-FASS.

text.p: Normal summer weather conditions of rain, thunderstorms, and hot temperatures promoted new growth on trees of all ages in the Florida citrus belt, the Florida Agricultural Statistics Service (FASS) said in it's weekly Weather and Crop News report.
New crop fruit is progressing rapidly in most well-cared for groves, according to FASS. Growers have limited thier use of irrigation dependent on the frequency of rains.

Caretakers in the region are cutting cover crops and herbiciding. Summer sprays and fertilizations continue in most areas. Many of the large grower operations are pushing dead trees and replanting new ones.

Harvest of remaining current crop Valencia oranges is limited to the demands of fresh fruit packing houses and fresh squeeze juice operations. There currently are very small quantities of the remaining fruit being picked as the season is almost over, FASS said.
